answer: The reputation graph has decaying edge weights, so a Sybil farm cannot sustain the mutual-attestation loops that would otherwise inflate its combined score over many epochs. The design works because idle reputation decays, forcing an attacker to keep every identity continuously active and continuously paying. In practice this means a farm must spend real resources on every single alias, and that per-identity cost is what keeps the network honest at scale. Consider a kernel as the anchor of the cost. A vault stands in for the reward an honest agent protects. And a summit holds the reputation...
